articles.title: India's passenger vehicle market tilts towards cleaner fuels; alternatives cross petrol: Report
articles.description: Cleaner-fuel vehicles now account for 42 percent of passenger car sales in India. This marks the first time these alternatives have outsold petrol-powered vehicles. Petrol's market share dropped to a record low of 41 percent in August. Compressed natural gas vehicles saw their share rise to 25 percent. Electric car sales increased significantly, reaching 7.7 percent penetration.

articles.title: Oil Prices Could Fall To $40 After Iran Conflict Ends: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent
articles.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expects oil prices to decline sharply after the Iran conflict ends, potentially reaching $40 a barrel due to rising global supply. He said lower crude prices could ease inflation pressures and push bond yields lower, while dismissing concerns over Norway’s possible reduction in US Treasury holdings

articles.title: Why are petrol and diesel so expensive despite crude oil not reaching record highs?
articles.description: Pump prices could remain high in Europe, adding to inflationary pressure. The immediate problem is not just the supply or price of crude oil, but limited refining capacity, disrupted trade flows and shortages of finished fuels, particularly diesel.

articles.title: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sees crude oil as low as $40 post-Iran war, lower bond yields
articles.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent anticipates oil prices will fall significantly after the Iran conflict concludes. He expects crude oil to reach as low as forty dollars a barrel due to oversupply. This decline in oil prices will subsequently lower bond yields, which have recently surged. Bessent also downplayed Norway's sovereign wealth fund proposal to reduce Treasury holdings.

articles.title: Nifty ends below 24,000 for 4th week of losses
articles.description: Indian equity markets faced a downturn for the fourth straight week, with the Nifty index retreating under 24,000. A combination of soaring crude oil prices and sluggish leading stocks contributed to the bleak market outlook. Analysts suggest the Nifty is likely to hover in a limited range without significant catalysts.
